newsitem.title: PORTUGAL: Portugal's Banco Pinto may be near peak.
newsitem.headline: Portugal's Banco Pinto may be near peak.

text.p: Portugal's Banco Pinto & Sotto Mayor (BPSM) has soared on optimism that a plan to "harmonise" operations between its banks will be speeded, but the shares may be reaching their peak, analysts said.
After gaining 23 percent in the past three weeks to trade at 1,390 escudos on Thursday, Banco Pinto may start to mark time awaiting confirmation the optimism was justified, they said.
"The buying must be linked to prospects for an acceleration in the restructuring of the group," said analyst Cristina Fonseca of ESR-Espirito Santo Research.

"(But) we will only see further sustained gains when it is known when, how much and exactly where the Champalimaud group will make its cost savings and see revenue growth (as a result of the restructuring)," said analyst Joao Capucho of Banco Finantia.
The sharp price gain for BPSM compares with an overall gain for the financial sector on the Lisbon bourse of four percent in the same period.

According to several analysts, the announcement on January 17 that Alipio Dias, chairman of Sotto sister bank Banco Totta & Acores (BTA), was standing down was interpreted by domestic investors as a sign the so-called "Harmony Project" would be speeded.

Banco Pinto & Sotto Mayor chairman Luis Champalimaud, son of the group's veteran chief, Antonio, now combines the top job at both banks. Dias had been seen as a fierce defender of Banco Totta's independence within the group.
The Champalimaud group announced last October that it intended to reorganise its banking interests to boost efficiency, centralising purchases and the banks' trading rooms, for example.
But analysts say that it was still unclear how the harmony project would work in practice.

"A restructuring such as Project Harmony only makes sense with a single entity at its head...that is why Sotto began to gain after the announcement that Dias was leaving," said one banking analyst in London.

Banco Sotto was also given a boost by the fact that its 1996 results, announced at the same time as Dias' resignation, were better than expected at 11.5 billion escudos, up from 7.6 billion the year before.
Banco Totta's results, in contrast, were worse than expected and the bank has subsequently taken a battering on the bourse.

"With the banking arm of the Champalimaud group restructured, it is Sotto that is going to gain most because it will be there that its owner (Antonio Champalimaud) will look for his biggest profit," said one analyst at a broker.
There was some switching by domestic investors out of Totta to Banco Sotto, traders said.
Analysts also noted that Banco Sotto would this year be able to consolidate 100 percent of Banco Chemical Portugal, which it bought in 1996, and this would also give a boost to its results for 1997.
"Despite not believing that BPSM is going to gain much more from here, the rise so far is not worrying on fundamental grounds," said another analyst who asked not to be identified.
